title: Multiprotocol session replayer with KV-cache-aware pacing for streaming completions
creator: Lena Park
description: Build a next-generation load harness that replays real user sessions across SSE and WebSocket endpoints while modelling KV cache state and prefix caching effects. Current tools simulate token throughput but do not capture cache-warmth-dependent tail latency patterns; this leads to blind spots when validating batching/kv-cache optimizations and regression detection for p95. The harness should: (1) replay recorded sessions (conversation histories) with probabilistic branching, (2) model KV cache hit/miss state per connection and support forced cold-start sequences, (3) support multiplexing many logical sessions over fewer physical connections to test connection pooling behaviors, (4) emit detailed telemetry aligned to production metrics (tokens/sec, p95/p99 by route/model, cache-hit-ratio, queueing time), and (5) integrate with our regression gate so nightly runs can fail PRs if p95 worsens beyond threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Can replay 50k concurrent logical sessions across SSE and WSS protocols with configurable multiplex factor
Supports KV cache state model (warm, partial-warm, cold) and can force sequences that exercise cache misses
Realtime telemetry for tokens/sec, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), queue depth, and cache-hit-rate emitted to Prometheus/Grafana
Integration with existing regression detector: harness produces canonical JSON artifacts consumed by runtime-regression-bot and can fail a GitHub Actions job when p95 regression > 5%
Runbook and ops dashboard available in Console (link in links) and documented in Confluence
End-to-end demo script that reproduces a known p95 regression from last quarter
approach: Design a session descriptor format (lightweight JSON) that includes token distribution, prefix length, branching probs, and cache-warmth flags
Extend current harness core to support two transport drivers: SSE and WebSocket with identical logical semantics; abstract streaming protocol layer
Implement a KV cache simulator that hooks into request lifecycle and records hit/miss timing impact; expose API to inject cache-miss spikes
Implement multiplexing layer: N logical sessions per connection with configurable interleaving and 'think time' distributions
Telemetry: map harness metrics to production metric names (redwood.inference.harness.*) and push to Prometheus pushgateway for nightly runs
Regression integration: produce summary JSON and histogram buckets compatible with runtime-1.21 regression detector; add GH Actions workflow that runs harness and posts results to PR
metrics: request_latency_ms percentiles p50/p95/p99 per route and per cache-state
cache_hit_rate (overall and by prefix length bucket)
test_scenarios: Baseline: 10k concurrent sessions, 1x multiplex, warm cache -> measure steady-state tokens/sec and p95
Cold-surge: 20% of sessions start cold simultaneously to simulate cache churn after deployment
Mix-protocol: 50/50 SSE vs WSS, multiplex factor 8, variable think-times drawn from production distribution
Burst: short 30s bursts to 100k logical sessions to exercise autoscaling and fallback routes
KV-degradation: inject artificial 2x latency on cache misses to observe p95 sensitivity
Regression-scan: run nightly against runtime-1.21 baseline and trigger PR gate when p95 > baseline*1.05
rollout_plan: MVP: deliver harness core + two simple session descriptors and KV simulator (week 1-2)
Expand scenarios and integrate Prometheus metrics (week 3)
Add multiplexing, GH Actions regression job, and Console dashboard (week 4)
Run a controlled experiment recreating last-quarter p95 regression and iterate on instrumentation (week 5)
Hand-off: runbook, demo video, and team training session; mark Done when nightly regression job is stable for 3 days
risks: Synthetic fidelity: replay engine may not fully capture complex user branching which could lead to false positives/negatives in regressions
Resource cost: large-scale runs (100k logical sessions) will be expensive; need to gate on off-peak cluster capacity
Instrumentation noise: mapping harness metrics to production names must be precise to avoid misattributing regressions
Protocol edge-cases: certain SDK client behaviors might not be reproduced, causing discrepancies vs real traffic
